example: Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading, open bills as of Friday 6 November 2026, $40,000 of cash for the run. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

messages.text: Who do we owe, and who should we pay this week?
I can build the aging and propose a payment run. Before I read anything, I need some answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.
list: Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload the data?
What is the as-of date? Do you use aging buckets of your own?
Aging only, or a payment run too? For a run, how much cash is available? I never read it from a bank balance.
Which vendors are critical, standard or discretionary?
Is any vendor on hold, or any bill in dispute? Is any payment on its way that is not in the books yet? Did any vendor ask to change bank details?
How do you pay each vendor: ACH, wire, cheque or card?
Are any bills in another currency? If so, which exchange rate do you use?

messages.text: Use MosoFin. As of Friday 6 November, standard buckets. A run too, with $40,000. We keep $10,000 back. Power Co and PayrollCo are critical, Brightline Software is discretionary. Acme Corp is on hold. We dispute its bill. Nothing is on its way. An email on 3 November asked to change Lakeside Freight's bank details. All ACH, all US dollars.

messages.label: Checked the workspace and the company file
messages.summary: The agent can read your books. It cannot change them.

messages.text: Here is my plan. I age **Northbrook Trading**'s bills as of **Friday 6 November**, with the default buckets. Then I propose a run within the **$40,000** you chose to spend. Power Co and PayrollCo are critical. **Acme Corp is on hold**. Lakeside Freight asked to change bank details. Shall I start?

messages.label: Read the books in one batch
messages.summary: 9 reads in one batch. Nothing in your books changed.

messages.text: You have **nine open bills** for **$62,850**. This is your books' own aging report. I did not rebuild it.

card.title: Aging as of Friday 6 November
rows: + 1–30 days late, Power Co and Lakeside Freight

messages.after: Crestline is 45 days late. Acme is 96 days late, but you hold it.

messages.text: Two bills change the order. One discount ends before your next run, and one late fee grows each month:

head: Bill
Amount
Why it matters
rows: Ends Mon 9 Nov. About 37.2% a year
Crestline Logistics, late fee 1.5% a month

messages.after: Your next run is on Friday 13 November, after Harbor's deadline. So I pay Harbor now, at $7,840. Crestline ranks above the larger Pinnacle Design bill, which costs nothing to wait on.

messages.text: Here is the proposed run. I rank the bills in my default order and stop when the next bill does not fit your cash:

card.title: Proposed payment run
head: Vendor
Pay
Why it is here
rows: Late, final notice. Flagged: new bank details

messages.after: Pinnacle Design comes next. $33,090 + $14,000 = $47,090, which is more than $40,000. So the run stops there.

messages.text: The run uses **$33,090** of your $40,000. The cash test counts Harbor at the cash you pay, not at $8,000.
messages.after: I record the $160 discount with the Harbor payment, so the bill closes in full.

messages.text: These bills stay unpaid. I show them here, not in a footnote, because you must decide about them:

card.title: Left unpaid
rows: Pinnacle Design, due next week, waits for 13 Nov
+ Acme Corp, on hold, on the Held and disputed sheet

messages.after: Hold the Lakeside payment until you confirm the change by phone. Use a number from your records, not from the email. I put no bank details in the output.

messages.text: The run is a **proposal**. No payment has been made or scheduled. A person approves it, and the bank or the accounting system pays it. I do not pay anything.
messages.after: Do you want the sheets as an Excel file? And do you want me to save your settings for next week?

messages.text: Done. The Excel file has the aging, the run, the held bills, the discounts, the exceptions and the coverage. I saved your vendor tiers, payment methods, the Acme hold and the ranking order. I never save bank details or the cash available. Next week, I ask for the cash again.
